# Temple Scroll Column 29 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 29 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 29:3 — "forever" vs. "in perpetuity"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "forever" | Simple, literal rendering |
| LOGOS | "in perpetuity" | More formal legal register |
| PNEUMA | "forever" | Simple, clear |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/PNEUMA: "forever." Clear, dignified, and avoiding the legal overtone of "in perpetuity."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/PNEUMA.

---

## 29:7 — "settle My glory" vs. "cause My glory to reside" vs. "fill it with My glory"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "settle My glory" | Literal rendering of the causative verb |
| LOGOS | "cause My glory to reside" | Preserves the causative (Hiphil) morphology |
| PNEUMA | "fill it with My glory" | Dynamic rendering emphasizing the result |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted a compromise: "cause My glory to dwell." Preserves the causative structure (LOGOS) while using "dwell" (shakhan, the root of Shekhinah) rather than "reside" for theological resonance. PNEUMA's "fill" imports a different Hebrew concept (male').

**Status:** Resolved with compromise.

---

## 29:7 — "for all days" vs. "for all time" vs. "forever"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "for all days" | Literal rendering of le-kol ha-yamim |
| LOGOS | "for all time" | Natural English equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "forever" | Simplified rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS: "for all time." Captures the temporal scope without EMET's overly literal phrasing or PNEUMA's loss of the distinctive Hebrew expression (different from le-olam, "forever").

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 29:9 — "set the land as holy" vs. "sanctify the land" vs. "make the land holy"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "set the land as holy" | Literal periphrastic rendering |
| LOGOS | "sanctify the land" | Formal English verb |
| PNEUMA | "make the land holy" | Simple dynamic phrasing |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS: "sanctify the land." Concise and theologically precise. PNEUMA's "make holy" is adequate but less elegant.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 29:13 — "the great sea" vs. "the Great Sea" vs. "the Mediterranean"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the great sea" | Literal, uncapitalized |
| LOGOS | "the Great Sea" | Capitalized as a proper geographical name |
| PNEUMA | "the Mediterranean" | Modern geographical name |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS: "the Great Sea." This is a proper biblical geographical term (ha-yam ha-gadol) and should be capitalized. PNEUMA's "Mediterranean" anachronistically imports modern geography.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 29:15 — "shall know" vs. "shall acknowledge" vs. "will come to know"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "shall know" | Literal rendering of yeda |
| LOGOS | "shall acknowledge" | Implies public recognition |
| PNEUMA | "will come to know" | Progressive process of recognition |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET: "shall know." The Hebrew yada encompasses knowledge, recognition, and acknowledgment. The simple "know" preserves this breadth of meaning.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 29:16 — "rule over them" vs. "reign over them"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "rule over them" | General term for authority |
| LOGOS | "reign over them" | Royal vocabulary appropriate for divine kingship |
| PNEUMA | "reign over them" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS/PNEUMA: "reign." "Reign" specifically connotes royal sovereignty, appropriate for the divine kingship theme.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/PNEUMA.

---
